# Overall Project Weekly Summary (Jun 21 - 27, 2026)

## Executive Summary
This week, Optimism focused on strengthening the Superchain’s security and preparing for the next generation of "fault proof" technology. We successfully resolved gas fee issues following a recent network upgrade and made significant progress in integrating advanced zero-knowledge math to make the network even more secure and scalable.

### Key Strategic Initiatives & Outcomes

**Enhancing Network Security and Reliability**
*Goal: To ensure the Superchain remains a safe and stable environment for users and developers.*
*   Updated security keys for the Foundation’s administrative accounts to maintain high-level protocol safety ([ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops#1479](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/pull/1479)).
*   Hardened the "Superchain Dependency Manager" through rigorous testing, ensuring that funds are correctly tracked and protected during complex transactions ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#21502](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21502)).
*   Cleaned up the network registry by removing old test networks, making the system easier for developers to navigate ([ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry#1263](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/pull/1263)).

**Improving the User and Developer Experience**
*Goal: To fix technical glitches that make it difficult or expensive for people to use the network.*
*   Identified and fixed a "gas estimation" bug on the Sepolia testnet that was causing transactions to fail unnecessarily after the Karst upgrade ([ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry#1259](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/pull/1259)).
*   Began integrating solar energy tokens into the ecosystem, expanding the Superchain's reach into real-world green energy assets ([ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io#1332](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/pull/1332)).

**Building Next-Generation Verification Technology**
*Goal: To use advanced "zero-knowledge" proofs to make the network faster and more decentralized.*
*   Reached a major milestone by integrating "kona-sp1," an experimental tool that uses advanced math to prove the network's state is correct without needing a central authority ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#21489](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21489)).
*   Finalized the design for "Proof-Carrying Data" (PCD), a new way for different parts of the blockchain to share verified information efficiently ([ethereum-optimism/specs#921](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/pull/921)).

### Cross-Repository Coordination
This week required tight synchronization across the entire stack to handle the aftermath of the **Karst Hardfork**.
*   **Gas Management:** Coordination between `superchain-registry`, `superchain-ops`, and `specs` was required to deploy configuration flags that fixed "intrinsic gas" errors reported by the community.
*   **Fault Proof Evolution:** The integration of the "Kona" project involved simultaneous updates to the core `optimism` monorepo, the technical `specs`, and the `superchain-registry` to ensure the new zero-knowledge verification tools work seamlessly with existing infrastructure.

## Repository Spotlights

### ethereum-optimism/optimism
*   Integrated **kona-sp1**, bringing experimental zero-knowledge fault proof capabilities to the OP Stack ([#21489](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21489)).
*   Completed a major "decoupling" effort to move core logic away from legacy Geth code, making the system more modular and easier to maintain ([#21487](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21487)).
*   Updated the global Go programming toolchain to version 1.26.4 to improve build reliability and performance ([#21452](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21452)).

### ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry
*   Introduced the `keep_karst_upgrade_gas` flag to fix transaction errors on Sepolia and Mainnet ([#1259](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/pull/1259)).
*   Refactored file writing processes to prevent errors when updating network data across different storage systems ([#1264](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/pull/1264)).

### ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops
*   Managed the migration of the Ink Sepolia network to the "OP Enterprise" framework ([#1478](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/pull/1478)).
*   Executed critical security rotations for the Foundation Upgrade and Operations safes ([#1479](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/pull/1479)).

### ethereum-optimism/specs
*   Finalized the technical blueprint for **Proof-Carrying Data (PCD)**, clearing the path for developers to start building this new scalability feature ([#21327](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/21327)).
*   Published new documentation and specifications to guide the community on how PCD will be integrated into the protocol ([#920](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/pull/920)).

### ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io
*   Resolved a high-priority issue where users were seeing "intrinsic gas too high" errors on the Sepolia testnet ([#21457](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/issues/21457)).
*   Advanced the development of **SafeDB**, a new way for the network to handle data that is more flexible and better suited for future upgrades ([#20278](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/issues/20278)).
